newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power eases with natgas, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power eases with natgas, weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were led softer Monday in light trading by mild weather and weakness in the natural gas spot market, industry sources said.

Firm, peak power into the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Tuesday delivery traded in the $20.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, down from last week's range of $21.00-23.00. Late deals were reported done as low as $18.50, market sources said.
Pressuring the market for the most part, traders said, was the falling natural gas prices to about $3.70 per million British thermal units on the Gulf Coast.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was assessed around $15.00, which is down marginally.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Tuesday delivery were around $21.00 per MWh, as compared with last week's $24.50 trades.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed around $16.00-16.50.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to be normal to slightly below-normal this week.
Separately, Duke Power said its three Oconee nuclear units in Seneca, S.C., with a combined generating capacity of 2,538 megawatts (MW), will likely resume power production in January.
Also, Tennessee Valley Authority's 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power plant returned to full power after last week's power reduction due to leaking condensor tubes.
